A flying buttress spanning forty feet between the outer ward and the keep, carved in the shape of a serpent mid-lunge, its stone scales reading clearly against pale limestone.
A crystal-spire erupting from the northeast tower, translucent violet and twice the keep's own height, refracting dawn light into colored shafts across the entire courtyard.
A bone-archway gate assembled from articulated dragon-vertebrae, each segment the size of a wagon wheel, bleached white against the dark iron portcullis behind it.
A dragon-skull mounted above the main gatehouse, lower jaw removed and replaced with a working portcullis, the eye-sockets fitted with iron-bracketed torch-baskets.
A floating tower tethered to the curtain wall by three thick iron chains, hovering visibly apart from the main structure, the gap between them reading as impossible negative space.
A waterfall channeled deliberately through the gatehouse archway, sheeting over the drawbridge platform in a continuous curtain, its white roar audible and visible from a mile off.
A drawbridge surfaced entirely with fitted skulls set in mortar, their hollow eye-sockets forming a dense pattern that reads as a cobblestone texture until you are ten feet away.
A hundred-foot carved-stone griffin gripping the top of the main gate-tower, its wingspan spanning the entire gatehouse roof and casting a recognizable silhouette from the valley below.
An obsidian-glass tower rising from the southwest corner, its mirror-black surface reflecting everything around it and creating a void-shaped absence in the castle's stone color.
A vine-overgrown spire at the eastern corner, the living growth so thick it has become a green cone shape indistinguishable from intentional topiary at first reading.
A machicolation row along the curtain wall built entirely from yellowed femur-shafts mortared in rows, their regular ivory color contrasting sharply with the grey stone beneath.
A stained-glass cathedral wall forming the entire southern face of the great hall, fifty feet of colored glass panels visible from the outer ward as a luminous patchwork.
A single tower twice the height of every other structure on the site, its isolation and vertical dominance making it read as a separate landmark rather than part of the castle.
A lava-moat running the full perimeter of the outer ward, its orange glow visible at night along the entire base of the curtain wall, defining the castle's footprint in fire.
An impossible cantilevered balcony jutting thirty feet from the keep's upper story with no visible support below, its thin silhouette reading as structurally wrong from every angle.
A Dwarven-rune-carved gateway with letters three feet tall cut deep into the stone arch face, the shadow-filled grooves making the runes readable at a hundred paces.
A colossal carved-relief of a serpent swallowing a sun covering the entire outer face of the curtain wall, its shallow relief lines readable only because they run a quarter-mile long.
A lattice glass-tower at the keep's northern corner, its open framework of iron and glass panels making it appear hollow and impossibly light against the solid stone around it.
A tree-integrated tower at the castle's rear, a living oak grown through the floor and out the roof so its crown rises above the parapet as a natural fifth spire.
A volcanic-glass spire capping the keep's highest point, its surface fractured into conchoidal facets that catch light differently from every angle, flickering against the grey stone mass below.
A dragon-tooth crenellation row running the full parapet of the outer ward, each merlon shaped into a curved fang three feet tall, giving the wall a jawline silhouette.
A spike-row of iron lances mounted along the curtain wall's outer face at regular intervals, each lance impaling a preserved skull, the row readable as a deliberate repeating pattern from distance.
An Elvish-leaf-pattern stonework arch framing the inner ward entry, the carved leaves so fine-detailed they register as organic texture rather than stone from more than twenty feet away.
A mirror-finish reflective spire sheathed in polished steel plates on the keep's central tower, its surface showing a warped reflection of the sky and making it read as cut-out light.
An acid-pit dry-moat surrounding the inner ward, the stone lip visibly corroded and pitted in long vertical streaks, the discoloration reading as evidence of something active and ongoing below.
